subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
This is the section about which I was speaking before dinner. It will be remembered that in the old section there were defined three classes of veterans who became eligible for allowances under the act. First of all, there were those who at the date of the proposed commencement of the allowance had attained the age of sixty. That was one class. Then there was another class who, in the opinion of the board, were permanently unemployable by reason of physical or mental disability. That was the second class. There was also a third class, who having served in a theatre of actual war had attained the age of fifty-five and were, in the opinion of the board, incapable of maintaining themselves

War Veterans' Allowance Act
because of disability, pre-aging, or general unfitness. My understanding of the intention of the legion convention at Fort William and of the resolution passed on that occasion, and also of what the minister intended to convey in his remarks on the resolution introducing this bill, was that the first two classes would be maintained as they now exist; and by the present section 3 that is done. The only difficulty or uncertainty or unsatisfactory condition
1	see is as to the third class. As I say, my impression of what was understood at Fort William was that the third class would be preserved very much as it existed except for the fact that the age limit of fifty-five would be swept away; in other words, those who were eligible only if they were fifty-five years of age would now be eligible irrespective of their age. I doubt whether the present section 4 which is being substituted for the old section 4 has that effect. I would refer to paragraph (c). In attempting to define this third class, section 4 provides:
Subject as hereinafter provided allowances under this act shall be payable with the approval of the board to any veteran who has been domiciled in Canada for the six months immediately preceding the date of the proposed commencement of the allowance, and who-
Then it defines classes one and two. Then in paragraph (c) it deals with the class I have described as the third; that is to say, it describes them as those who do not qualify by age or disability under the two preceding paragraphs, but having served in a theatre of actual war are, in the opinion of the board, incapable and unlikely to become capable of maintaining themselves because of economic handicaps combined with physical or mental disability or insufficiency.
The point I would make is that in the old definition no regard was had to the question whether the applicant was likely to become capable of maintaining himself. The sole question for determination was whether he was or was not capable of maintaining himself. Those words, "unlikely to become capable of maintaining himself," introduce a restrictive feature which was not heralded in the remarks the minister made on the resolution, and was not the understanding of the convention at Fort William. I suggest that the intention of all parties in the house would be carried out if the words, "and unlikely to become capable," were omitted.
Then I am very much afraid that subsection
2	clips the wings of the board almost entirely in dealing with the third class to which I have reference. Subsection 2 now reads:
The provisions of paragraph (c) of subsection 1-
And paragraph (c) of subsection 1 is the paragraph which would let in this third class. -shall not be construed to apply to any veteran who is, in the opinion of the board, physically and mentally capable of maintaining himself if work were available.
My submission is that many of these burnt-out veterans for whom this legislation is designed, while not capable of performing a hard day's work, a full day's work, and for that reason unable to compete successfully in the labour market, are nevertheless capable of maintaining themselves if work of a certain kind is available. For instance, many of them could maintain themselves as elevator operators, night watchmen, caretakers, timekeepers, if such work were available. But of course there are very few such jobs available. It seems to me that by that subsection we are not only making it possible for the board to refuse allowances to men in that category but actually tying the hands of the board, preventing the board from giving relief in many cases in which relief should be given. It seems to me that the board will have to ask itself, if work were available, Could this man maintain himself? As I say, a man might be capable of maintaining himself as an elevator operator or caretaker or in some other form of sheltered employment if it were available. If the board decided that he was fitted for that type of work, it seems to me that they would be compelled to refuse him the allowance.
I should also like to hear from the minister as to subsection 3, which provides that an allowance shall not be awarded or continued to a veteran while such veteran is in receipt of an old age pension. That comes as somewhat of a surprise. I do not think there was any mention at Fort William of a provision of that sort, and I do not think legislation containing such a provision can be said to fulfil to the utmost the requests of the returned soldiers themselves as expressed through the dominion convention of the Canadian Legion held at Fort William'. I am hoping that the minister will be able to dispense with that provision.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
In endorsing the remarks of the hon. member for London (Mr. Betts), I would point out that when the special committee on returned soldiers' problems considered this paragraph so carefully two years ago, we expressly distinguished between veterans permanently unemployable and temporarily unemployable, the idea being that a man of fifty-five to sixty need not show that he was permanently unemployable. I suggest that the intention is to give the board very
War Veterans' Allowance Act

wide discretion, and that these words, "unlikely to become capable," in paragraph (c) should be cut out, and subsection 2 be cut out also. There will be then no question at all of the powers of the board, and we need have no fear that the act will not be fairly administered.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Will the minister be good enough to outline how the board would iproceed to determine eligibility under paragraph (c) of subsection 1? How would he define "economic handicaps"?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Possibly a man who has
not had a job for four or five years and could not get one; that would perhaps be an economic handicap. I do not like attempting to define these things. The trouble with most of our pension legislation has been that we have defined either too much or too little. If we define too much we sometimes let in a large class of people who are not entitled at all. If we restrict the powers of the boards or commission and do not allow them the widest possible discretion, many hardships are incurred.
It has nothing to do with this, but by way of digression may I say that if at the inception of this pension legislation we had appointed a board, such as the veterans' allowance board, and given them the widest possible discretion in the awarding of pensions, I think we would not have got into all the snarls that we have since been in with respect to pension legislation. Every time we introduce legislation which specifies distinctly a class or classes we get into trouble, either by excluding someone or by including too many. The officers of the department and myself have given a great deal of thought to the phraseology of this section for the past four or five months, we have written and rewritten it not once but many times, and this is the best we can submit to the committee. I have no objection whatever to any hon. member trying his hand at drafting, and if he can make a better job I am quite willing to adopt it. It must be borne in mind, however, that this is not a relief measure, it is not intended to give relief to people who are only temporarily out of employment. That is a municipal and provincial matter. There would be no proper way for this department to administer an act which provided that a man would get the allowance for a short period of time merely because he is out of work. This is intended to deal with people who are burnt-out, and we have purposely made it as broad as possible, leaving the fullest possible discretion to the members of the board.
^Mr. Green.]

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Would the minister consider inserting the word "fully" before the words "physically and mentally capable," so that it would read, "who is, in the opinion of the board, fully physically and mentally capable"?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
In the first place I think it would not be good English, although I have not much regard for literature in making legislation. But I do not think it would help.
If he is physically and mentally capable, I suggest he is fully physically and mentally capable.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: No; he might be physically and mentally capable of running an elevator, but not of doing heavy manual work.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I do not think the word "fully" should go in there.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Does the
expression, "theatre of actual war," in paragraph (c) include England?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: No.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Or the
ocean?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
No. In the act "theatre of actual war " in the naval force is described in this way:
In the case of the naval forces, the high seas or wherever contact has been made with hostile forces of the enemy, or wherever the veteran has sustained injury or contracted disease directly by a hostile act of the enemy.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
What about the Royal
Canadian Air Force? Is not England an " actual theatre " for them?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: We can determine from the War Office whether it is or not, according to the nature of their service. The War Office has laid down certain regulations.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I know there were men on the North Sea patrol who were stationed all the time on the island.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes, quite true.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Was much difficulty experienced by the board in complying with and construing the definition in the former act? I refer to the definition which reads:
-in the opinion of the board, incapable of maintaining himself because of disability, preaging and general unfitness, and in either case is-
And so on.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Perhaps I am not quite clear, but do I understand the hon. member to suggest that we should use the phraseology of the former act, and leave out only the

War Veterans' Allowance Act
words " fifty-five "? Does he believe the phraseology of the former act is preferable to the suggested phraseology?

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I have not expressed an opinion.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I am asking, purely for the sake of information, and to gain assistance.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If that is as far as the minister will go, I would say that that definition would, in my opinion, be preferable to the one now suggested. But the suggestion I make is that the words, "unlikely to become capable," be dropped. At the risk of repeating myself, I would say my objection to the section as it now stands is that in the former definition no attention was paid to what was going to become of the veteran in the future. That was not a matter which came under consideration by the board at all. The question for determination was: Is he capable now of maintaining himself? By introducing the words, " unlikely to become capable," I suggest we are narrowing the clause.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I am not prepared to agree that we are narrowing the clause by the language used in the amendment. But perhaps this might appeal to the committee: In the case of a man who has just suffered a broken leg, I do not think it is the intention of the committee-certainly it is not the intention of the board-that he shall be eligible under the act. There must be some kind of permanency, and the word "likely" does not bar him! Surely the board has the right to use its discretion as to whether he is likely. Perhaps that is not a good word; it may not be a proper expression, but certainly it means probability. I think all hon.. members will agree that there should not be any intention of making a person eligible who has a mere temporary disability.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
I have read the section
carefully and have listened to the observations of the hon. member for London. It does seem to me that it divides itself into three classes, and the governing word in the third class is the word "combined." First, the veteran gets an allowance if he is sixty years of age. Second, if he is not sixty years of age, but in the opinion of the board is unemployable, permanently, because of physical and mental disability, he gets consideration. The third case refers to any age, but not qualifying for age or disability provided under the two preceding paragraphs. However he has served in a theatre of war, and in the opinion of the board is incapable or unlikely to become capable of maintaining himself, because of economic handicaps, combined
with physical or mental disability or insufficiency. That certainly makes the physical or mental disability or insufficiency the governing factor, when linked with the other provisions of that subsection. I cannot see it any other way.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: He has to have all those things.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes; as the section reads, apparently he has to have all those things. Is that the intention of the government?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
It is intended to apply
to a man with partial disability, but who, as well, has certain economic handicaps.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: But it must be combined with physical or mental disability or insufficiency. The word "combined" would worry me.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
He should really have the
two; he should be incapable of obtaining work, owing to his physical or mental insufficiency.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
The economic handicap is
his incapacity to obtain work owing to his physical or mental incapacity. The danger in making this section too broad would be that immediately it would be used by every veteran out of employment. It is not intended that that man should be covered. I am free to admit, as I have already done, that this is a most difficult clause to draft, and I would welcome assistance from anybody.
The only thing I can do is suggest to the committee that, in view of the manner in which the War Veterans' Allowance Act has been administered in the past, and in view particularly of the manner in which this particular section has been administered since 1936, it might take my present recommendation. Hon. members will recall that there were some doubts as to just what the language meant, and under what category veterans would come, in view of the language then proposed. But I am quite free to say that apart from what I might call the first rush of applications from people who had the idea, through newspaper reports, that every veteran over fifty-five yeai's was eligible, the board has had no difficulty whatsoever in administering the section as it stood after the 1936 amendment. It is for that reason I am convinced that we must allow the widest possible discretion to the board, and it seems to me that we should not load on their shoulders the onus of having discretion in refusing people who quite clearly should not be entitled, owing to the fact
War Veterans' Allowance Act

that, although they are out of employment, they are not suffering from other tangible or intangible disability. It is the best we can do, under the circumstances, by way of language.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
How would the minister
like this:	"Does not qualify by age or disability under the two preceding paragraphs, but having served in a theatre of actual war,
is,	in the opinion of the board, suffering from such physical or mental disability or insufficiency as renders him incapable of maintaining himself."

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
That was the wording we
had at one time, but I forget why we changed
it.	I need not tell the right hon. gentleman that the section was written and rewritten; many drafts were torn up. However, I have no objection to considering the suggested wording.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: There are three paragraphs in this section, but paragraph (c) is the only one which specifies that a man must have served in a theatre of war. Am I right in supposing that this stipulation does not apply to those coming under paragraph (a) and (b) ?

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: The definition of "veteran" covers that.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: The definition would cover that. The only man eligible under the War Veterans' Allowance Act is the man who served in a theatre of actual war, with the exception that if a man has obtained a pension, even though he served only in Canada, he would be eligible.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Then, why put those words in the paragraph? They are superfluous and calculated to make one misunderstand it.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: It is to cover the man who does not qualify by age or disability but who has served in a theatre of actual war. On that account, because of his service, he is entitled to come under the provisions of the act without having to be either permanently unemployable or sixty years of age.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: You have stated that "veteran" means a man who served in a theatre of war, and it seems to me superfluous to find it again in paragraph (c). It gives the impression that service in a theatre of war applies only to paragraph (c). If a veteran is defined in the act to mean a man who served in a theatre of war, what is the need of mentioning that service in paragraph (c) ?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: The principal thing was to make it clear to the soldiers themselves that only those who served in a theatre of war would be eligible.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Why not put it in (a) and (b) ?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That is well understood in connection with (a) and (b). I do not want there to be any doubt in the mind of anyone as to those benefiting having served in a theatre of actual war.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That is just what I want to avoid and I suggest that it should be in (a) and (b). That will be the first question asked.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: We cannot put it in <a) and (b) because some of those men may be pensioners.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I think we are all agreed that what we are aiming at is to take care of the 5,100 odd veterans who served in a theatre of actual war, who are unemployed and are wholly or partly unfit.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Quite.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Many of these men may be only forty or forty-five years of age, and it would obviously be unfair to insist that the board must find that such a man is unlikely to be capable of working again. We all hope the younger men in this group will be capable of working again. Surely the department is amply protected by the two provisions that an applicant must be suffering from economic handicaps-in other words, he must have been out of work for two or three years-and in addition must have a physical or mental disability or insufficiency. Surely those qualifying words are strict enough; they go a good deal further than the recommendations of the veterans' assistance commission.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: There is nothing strict about the word at all. With the provisions as suggested by my hon. friend, a man who had an acute case of pneumonia would be qualified, and that is the man we do not want to qualify. There must be some degree of permanency about it. I think the committee will understand that we could not hope to administer this act with men going on and off as they obtained employment. This is legislation for the burnt-out veteran, and the implication is that those who qualify are no longer able to work or are not in a position to hope ever to work. I do not want to go quite that far and I do not think it will be interpreted in that way, but I certainly want to avoid having the benefits go to those who are only temporarily unemployed.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Would paragraph (c) cover a man who was incapable of continuing in his ordinary occupation or vocation? I have in mind a farmer who is a returned man

143S
War Veterans' Allowance Act
but whose health does not permit him to do the heavy work of farming. Would he be expected to go away from home to look for some easier work?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If he is not capable of any gainful employment he would be eligible.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I do not think that answers my question. As someone said this afternoon, he might be capable of running an elevator, but to get such employment he would have to leave home and go fifty miles away to a town or city. Would he be expected to leave his family?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That would be his economic handicap. That is why those words are in the section. *

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: "Incapable of maintaining himself at his ordinary occupation"- is that the way it would be interpreted?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes, broadly speaking.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I should likp to inquire as to the eligibility of a man, say forty-five or forty-nine years of age, the average age, who is too old to be accepted in the employment for which he has been trained. The minister is well aware that a large number of veterans are considered to be too old to continue in employment in certain important industries in this country. Would the fact that they are unable bo resume the vocation for which they were trained qualify them under this clause?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If a man of forty-five was as physically fit as a man of that age would normally be, he would not be eligible under this clause even though there was no work available at the moment.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
How would the minister think this would do in place of paragraph (c) ? We have dealt with paragraphs (a) and (b), and could we not say this:
(c) does not qualify by age or disability under the two preceding paragraphs, but having served in a theatre of actual war, is, in the opinion of the board, suffering from such physical or mental disability or insufficiency as would entitle him to such allowance if he were not disqualified by reason of age and otherwise as provided by the preceding subsections.
I have not written it out, but I just wanted to get the sense of it. This is the comprehensive clause as it covers every class not covered by the two preceding paragraphs. It has the one rider, namely, physical or mental disability or insufficiency in the opinion of the board. That is, first of all the board must satisfy
itself that the man is not sixty years of age; second, that he is not permanently unemployable because of physical or mental disability.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That means total disability.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Permanent unemployability means total incapacity. Let us take the third paragraph, which covers everything:
Does not qualify by age or disability under the two preceding paragraphs, but having served in a theatre of actual war, is, in the opinion	of	the	board,	suffering	from	such
physical or mental disability or insufficiency as would entitle him to an allowance to the same extent as though he was qualified under the two preceding paragraphs of this section.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: May I just repeat it.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Here it is:
Does not qualify by age or disability under the two preceding paragraphs, but having served in a theatre of actual war, is, in the opinion	of	the	board,	suffering	from	such
physical or mental disability or insufficiency as would entitle him to the benefits of this allowance were it not for the provisions of paragraphs (a) and (b).

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Perhaps if I repeated it- " Is in the opinion of the board suffering from such physical or mental disability-"

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Or insufficiency.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: "-or insufficiency to such an extent as would qualify him-"

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes, under the preceding paragraphs, if it were not for the restriction of age or permanent disability. Is that too broad?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: No; I do not think it is broad enough.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That covers every case except those two.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I shall be glad to read it in Hansard, but I think it would narrow it. Did I understand my right hon. friend to say it would cover the economic handicap?

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I think it covers everything. It is intended to cover every other kind of case that would qualify him were it not for the distinct provisions of (a) and (b); that is, his lack of age, his lack of permanent disability. Then if he is physically unfit and mentally unfit, he would be entitled to the allowance as though he fell within (a) and (b) but for the disqualification of age and permanent incapacity which he is not suffering.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
The first difficulty I see is over the word "suffering." That would imply medical examination of some kind. We would have to change that language, for the idea is to get away as far as possible from medical
War Veterans' Allowance Act

examination. We hope there will be no necessity for medical examination except so far as to exclude the man as being fit under the next subsection, but I shall be very glad to let this section stand and come back to it on another occasion.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Perhaps we will sit down
and write a section before the next sitting.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Will the minister give us his opinion about the veterans' allowance in connection with old age pension. Cannot he make provision that the amount shall be only less any amount he receives from old age pension?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
No; I think this is all right. I do not think there is any danger of the man being deprived of his old age pension or of this allowance, but I think we are all in agreement that he should not have the two. The paragraph reads:
An allowance shall not be awarded or continued under this act to a veteran or a recipient while such veteran or recipient is in receipt of an old age pension.
If he is in receipt of an old age pension and prefers to come under our act, all he has to do is to abandon the old age pension and we will give him the allowance; but what we will not do, and do not propose to do, is to allow him to come under our act and also allow him to draw $10 under the old age pension in addition to $10 under this act. As the members of the committee know, there is an exemption up to $240, which is counted as exempted income. Cases have arisen where a man drawing $20 under the War Veterans' Allowance Act maintains he has a right to draw $10 more from the provincial government in old age pension, and some provincial governments were only too glad to show their generosity when they were dealing with seventy-five per cent of somebody else's money, some insisting that they be allowed to give the man this $10. Our reply was: "All right, you can give him the whole amount, and we will not give him the war veterans' allowance."

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
I have known a case where a man's application for war veterans' allowance was refused, and he was told: "You are seventy years of age; go and take the old age pension." There would be that disposition. The words in the section are:
An allowance shall not be awarded or continued-
They may say: "You are in receipt of an old age pension, and therefore you will receive nothing under this act."

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
If he wants to fool us he
can drop his old age pension and come to us and say: " Please give me the war veterans' allowance."

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: And the provincial government may aid him in doing so.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That is what will inevitably happen.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
We did. not think of it in
1930 when the act was first passed; but had parliament of that day known that old age pensions would be extended on such a scale as they have been, arrangements would have been made so that anybody qualifying for old age pension at the age of seventy would go on the old age pension and not have the war veterans' allowance.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Too near an election at
that time.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Possibly, and no amendments were made after the election. Of course, there was always the hope that there would be an early and successful appeal to the people. At the present time, when the federal government is paying a war veterans' allowance to people who are entitled to war veterans' allowance and to people who are entitled to old age pension, I suppose if we shifted them on to the province we would save twenty-five per cent, but there has been never any disposition of that kind under any administration.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
No; it has always been
regarded as our responsibility under defence.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
There is no intention that
this section will be used to force veterans onto the old age pension?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: No, the other way round.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Is "maintaining himself"
interpreted to mean under the old section maintaining himself and dependents or maintaining himself only?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
It had some reference to
dependents.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Before we leave paragraph
(c) of section 3, the minister said that his main preoccupation was to give the board the most unfettered, the widest possible discretion. I think we all want that. He also said that under the former section which it is now proposed to repeal, after the first rush of applications that came in there was very little difficulty experienced by the board in dealing with the applications and in construing the legislation. I would point out that under the former definition all that the

War Veterans' Allowance Act
board had to do was to form an opinion that the applicant, provided he was fifty-five, was incapable of maintaining himself because of disability, pre-ageing and general unfitness. The board had to form no opinion whatever as to what would become of the applicant in the future, as to the probability of the applicant being unable to maintain himself in the future. But by amending the section in the manner proposed we are casting on the board the necessity of making up its mind in every case whether the applicant will be capable of maintaining himself in the future. So the minister is doing just what he says he does not want to do, hampering and fettering the board, clipping their wings.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
We say, "if in the opinion
of the board." We do not fetter or hamper them. We say: "If a man is, in the opinion of the board, incapable and unlikely to become capable." The board decides whether he is likely or unlikely to become capable of maintaining himself.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
The minister is asking the
board to decide something it was not required to decide before, the probability of the applicant becoming capable or incapable. That is an added restriction on the board. That is my objection.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If the minister is not willing to change paragraph (c) of subsection 1, would he consider wiping out subsection 2, which further restricts the board?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I do not think I can consider wiping out subsection 2. That is the safeguarding provision to prevent this from being an unemployed relief act.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes, but the minister said with regard to paragraph (c) that economic handicaps meant, for example, that a man had been out of work for, say a year. Yet subsection 2 is contradictory. It says, "physically and mentally capable of maintaining himself if work were available". The two do not fit in. I suggest that subsection 2 come out. The department is amply protected by the wide terminology of paragraph (c). [DOT]

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I would not like to ask the board to carry on under this act without having at least this safeguard in it, to make it quite clear that it is not the intention of parliament that mere lack of work would be a qualification.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: But you have also the qualification in paragraph (c) that the veteran must be "unlikely to become capable of maintaining himself". If that is left in, surely it is sufficient protection.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I am sorry, but I cannot agree.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: How would this affect a farmer on some marginal land who is incapable of working the farm himself? Would he be allowed to turn the farm over to his son to maintain himself?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I suppose that if his action were construed as fraud or evasion, he would not be eligible. But otherwise I imagine

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: He could not run the farm himself, and if it is sub-marginal land he could not afford to hire a man to work for him. Would he not be eligible for the allowance?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Some men who are on farms are now in receipt of veterans' allowance, and some deduction is made owing to the fact that such a man is not obliged to pay rent and he gets some subsistence from his farm. But there is a section in the act, section 8, which states that when it appears to the board that-
-any veteran has made a voluntary assignment or transfer of property for the purpose of qualifying for an allowance or for a larger allowance than he might otherwise have been entitled to receive, the income derivable from such property shall, in determining the allowance, if any, which such veteran should receive, be taken in account as if the assignment or transfer had not been made.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Will the minister explain what procedure will be followed to determine what degree of physical or mental disability or insufficiency would enable a man to qualify? Would the man be subjected to an examination? The reason I ask is this-

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: He would have to have a medical examination to determine whether he is fit. I have already said that.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Will the pre-aging be a definite factor?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: In tangible or intangible handicaps. What an intangible handicap is I do not know; I cannot define it. But if a man is not just able to work or cannot hold a job because his physical and mental condition is such that he is not capable of doing it, then he comes under the act. I cannot explain it any more than that. If it is just a case of his being out of work because the mill or the plant is closed down, he does not come under it.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Or if he is lazy.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
The Minister of Finance says that if he is lazy he does not come under it. I say unfortunately in most cases he does.
War Veterans' Allowance Act

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: As the minister has intimated that it is his intention to reserve this section for further consideration, despite his opinion as expressed this evening in answer to questions of the hon. member for Yale, I am going to ask the minister to reconsider the views he has expressed with respect to the interpretation given by the justice department to the words, "served in an actual theatre of war."

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Will my hon. friend try his hand at drafting something to cover his case, and I shall see what I can do.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes, I shall be very glad to do so. I do not know whether it was last session or the session before that I personally went before a committee of the house over which the minister was presiding, and I thought I had the minister's sympathetic consideration of the situation. One of the cases I then had in mind was that of a sergeant who had been on conducting parties and had actually been under fire. There is no necessity of my repeating the circumstances as the minister is thoroughly familiar with the facts; but I feel that, in view of some cases which have come to my attention, and as we are now extending this war veterans' allowance to practically the limit to which it can be extended,- an injustice is done in many cases by adhering to the interpretation given by the justice department. I welcome the suggestion of the minister and I shall try my hand at drafting something to meet the situation.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: In any case the bill will not pass this evening; certain sections of it have been held over, and I shall be glad to consider any amendment which my hon. friend suggests. But I warn him that I would not like him to make it so broad as to cover those who have not actually had fairly meritorious service.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Oh, yes.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
But if the man is an
enlisted man acting under orders and he is a casualty, surely he should be entitled to it.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: This factor has to be taken into account: The Department of National Defence decided which men were to have medals. I think that is perhaps the determining factor in this whole situation; and as I understand, conducting officers were not awarded the victory medal. The election men should have been awarded a victory medal, because they won the election, but I do not know about the war.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: That is another feature.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: After all, the test should be, Was he an enlisted man; if he was an enlisted man, did he suffer a disaster in a theatre of war?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Well, he did not. This man did not suffer disaster during the war. This is not a wounded man.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: The one I am talking about is one who did. It was in a minor capacity.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I believe that those who did suffer any disability in a theatre of actual war would be pensionable.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I should think so.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
He is eligible under the
War Veterans' Allowance Act if he suffered injury. But this is the case of a man who suffered no injury whatever; he had a short and rather uneventful service, in that he crossed over in one case conducting troops, as a conducting officer.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Was he an enlisted man?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Presumably he was an officer.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: He was a sergeant. My recollection is that he actually did suffer some injury, but I would not like to state that for a certainty.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If he had any injury due to his war service or to service in the army during the war he would be entitled to a pension.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
No, because he cannot
prove his present incapacity is attributable to the injury.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Ah, that is another point. But I imagine if he had any injury incurred on or attributable to service, he would have entitlement under the Pension Act.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
That has always been
my understanding.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
And there would be no
difficulty about getting war veterans' allowance. But as I understand it, this is the case of a man who is now disabled owing to illness or to incapacity which has occurred since the war.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Not necessarily referable to his wounds.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Not referable to his wounds at all. That man is not entitled normally to the benefits of this act. But as I said, I should like to consider the matter. There

War Veterans' Allowance Act
cannot be very many such cases. I should like to consider an amendment which would not broaden the act to the extent of covering persons who did not serve' in a theatre of war, yet might cover cases such as are mentioned by my hon. friend.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
We have been wandering
more or less all over section 4 of the act, which, is being amended, and as the minister is going to reconsider various subsections, I suggest that subsection 3 might work a hardship on the married man. This subsection provides that the allowance shall not be awarded or continued under the act to a veteran or the recipient of an old age pension.	As is well known, the old age
pension is $20 a month, and, if a man is married $40. But if, as is usually the case, there is a gap of five or ten years between the ages of husband and wife, it might happen that refusal to give the veterans' allowance to a married man might reduce his potential income by half. I do not believe there is provision for a man who is drawing the old age pension to waive it.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes. The moment he drops it he is eligible.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: So long as it is clearly established that he may do so, it is all right. This subsection says that the allowance cannot be awarded or continued-

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
"While such veteran or
recipient is in receipt of an old age pension.''

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
It is clearly the intention
that a man need not sacrifice $40 a month because he is already in receipt of $20?

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Can he be allowed to give
up the $20?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Before leaving section 3 I
hope that the minister will see fit to drop, or at any rate to modify, subsection 2. However, if he does not do so, I believe he will agree with me that we ought to endeavour to write king's English into the statutes. I am no purist, but in subsection 2, it seems to me, if I may trust my ear, we have made a mistake, and I am ashamed to say I do not know whether it is in mood or tense. Let me read it:
The provisions of paragraph (c) of subsection one shall not he construed to apply to any veteran who is, in the opinion of the board, physically and mentally capable of maintaining himself if work were available.
My submission is that "were" is not correct; it should be "be" or "is." There are some schoolmasters in the chamber. Perhaps they can tell us.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
I am informed that this
very point was submitted to the law clerk- though I refuse to accept the authority of the law clerk on this particular point-who stated that "were" was good English. Personally I think it is, but I shall not start a controversy with my hon. friend. If he can find an authority among the schoolmasters in the chamber justifying the change to "be" or "is," I shall be glad to consider the suggestion.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Can the minister tell us
by what method economic handicaps are measured? In committee we endeavoured to devise a formula to deal with the industrially unfit. In disqualifying those who are physically and mentally capable of maintaining themselves where work is available, no reference is made to the particular vocation for which such men have been trained. I submit that subsection 2 imposes too severe a restriction, because there are men who are industrially unfit to undertake work of a sort that might be available; that work might be such as they could not be reasonably expected to perform, and yet it could not be said that work had been absolutely denied them.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
If he has a disability or
if he is suffering from an insufficiency he is qualified for consideration.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
You cannot go much
further than "insufficiency."

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I am. referring to the restriction contained in subsection 2. "Physically and mentally capable of maintaining himself if work was available" seems to me to contradict the intention of paragraph (c) of subsection 1. The ex-service men would like some assurance that this deals with those commonly designated as the industrially unfit.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: It is no use trying to get me into a hole on this. What the ex-service men wanted was provision with respect to men who were out of work, and this is not intended to. cover men who are simply not employed. My hon. friend will remember the discussions in the committee, and there is no question that representations were made to cover people who were unemployed without any question whatever of disability. This bill is not intended for that purpose.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext:
Inasmuch as "economic handicaps" is not defined, the minister might perhaps insert some such words as these: "Lack of opportunities provided by the economic system, combined with. . . .".
War Veterans' Allowance Act

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Is there any set amount which the board considers sufficient for a man to maintain himself. Suppose he has an income of $150; would that preclude him from the war veterans' allowance?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: The act fixes a maximum of $730 for a married man.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If he received $200 from some other source he could still receive the war veterans' allowance?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: We allow him the maximum including that. There are a very large number who are receiving $10 a month pension and they still receive the war veterans' allowance.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Will a nursing sister who is married, whose husband is out of employment and who is otherwise eligible, be allowed to qualify?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: There is no double standard. The nursing sister who is married is as much entitled to support her husband as her husband is entitled to support her. I do not see any difficulty about that.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Suppose a man was entitled to assistance under the act but died before he had either applied for or received assistance: would his widow .be entitled to temporary assistance?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: No.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: I understood the minister to say that the maximum receivable under the War Veterans' Allowance Act was $40 for a man and his wife, and that earnings were permitted up to $250.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Would that $250 include a pension?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: Anything.

subtopic: EXTENSION OF ALLOWANCES TO INCLUDE CERTAIN OTHER CLASSES-ENLARGEMENT OF MEMBERSHIP OF BOARD
speechtext: If he received a pension of $250, thj,t would be his maximum?

Right Hon. ERNEST LAPOINTE (Minister of Justice) moved the second reading of Bill No. 36, to amend the Penitentiary Act.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: COMPUTATION OP TIME SERVED BY CONVICTED PRISONERS PENDING APPEAL
speechtext:
This bill has only one clause and it is very simple. It reads:
1. Subsection four of section forty-four of the Penitentiary Act, chapter one hundred and fifty-four of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1927, as enacted by section nine, chapter twenty-seven of the statutes of 1932-33, is repealed and the following substituted therefor:
"(4) Subject to the provisions of subsection two of section one thousand and nineteen of the criminal code, any period during which a convict is detained in the gaol or other place of confinement pursuant to the authority of this section shall not be computed as time served in the execution of his sentence, unless he be so detained pending an appeal by the attorney general or counsel for the crown."
While section 1019 of the criminal code states that this is subject to any direction
Canada Evidence Act

the court of appeal may make to the contrary, the amendment is merely to add to the section ini the Penitentiary Act the words, "subject to the provisions of subsection 2 of section 1019 of the criminal code." The intention is to harmonize the two.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: COMPUTATION OP TIME SERVED BY CONVICTED PRISONERS PENDING APPEAL
speechtext:
Perhaps this affords me an opportunity to make one observation I should like the minister to consider. Some months ago there was a criminal trial in the county of Renfrew. Upon an appeal being taken, the court ordered a new trial in any event, and the execution that had been ordered was of course vacated. But no judgment has been given on the question as to whether or not the case should not be discharged on the ground that there, in any event, was no evidence to go to a jury. This matter is causing a good deal of comment, because it has been long delayed.
I do not know that the minister can do anything, but I suggest that in a case of this kind it might be desirable to do something to expedite the delivery of judgment. This is now the month of March, and it is a long time since the trial took place. I venture to mention this now because this bill may be the only vehicle which would enable me to do so. I had intended to do it at some other time, but perhaps the minister would go into the matter to see if something can be done to have judgment given without further delay.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT
speechtext: This is to add to the exceptions under section 4 of the Canada Evidence Act one whereby the wife or husband may be a competent and compellable witness, one against the other, when one is charged for the theft of property belonging to the other.

subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT
speechtext: While they are living apart.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT
speechtext: Yes, when they are living apart. This has been recommended by some magistrates, and more particularly by the late commissioner of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Already there are eight cases excepted from the general rule, and this will be another one. For instance, witnesses may be compellable one against the other in cases of seduction, vagrancy, the abandonment of a child, and so on. I believe this is a proper change to make.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT
speechtext: It really extends the exceptions to the general rule that the husband and wife are one, and permits either to be called against the other where one has stolen from the other while they have been living apart.

subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT
speechtext: I do not know. Under our own law they are competent and compellable when one or the other is charged with an infamous offence, such as seduction, vagrancy, neglect to provide the necessaries of life, the abandonment of a child under two years, unlawful carnal knowledge, rape, bigamy and abduction. I do not know whether under the English law this provision appears.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: HUSBAND OR WIFE COMPETENT WITNESSES IN CERTAIN PROSECUTIONS-SUBMISSION OF CERTAIN PROOF OF AFFIDAVIT
speechtext: I think so, although I am only speaking subject to correction. This suggestion has been made more particularly by Mr. J. W. McFadden, K.C., crown attorney in Toronto, who wrote me as follows:
Section 29 of the evidence act should be redrafted. Our courts are flooded with prosecutions of eases where bad cheques are given. Some of these cheques are given on banks ranging from Halifax to Vancouver. Most of

Royal Canadian Mounted Police
these cheques are for small amounts. We cannot go to the cost of bringing a banker but by section 29 we are able to prove the statement of the man's account by affidavit. The section, however, is deficient in that it only provides for cases where the man has got some account in the bank. Where, however, cheques have been given and there is no account at all there is no provision made and the consequence is that we cannot think of launching a prosecution.
I have taken this matter up with Mr. Rogers, secretary of the bankers' association, and he is quite alive to the necessity of some amendment. Some time ago I drafted an affidavit for use in the courts. This has been a real boon to bankers in that they are not wasting three or four mornings in court and incidentally it has saved the city several hundreds of dollars in money. Where, however, there is no account we still have to subpoena these bankers.
This is to make the law apply when there is nothing in the books showing an account, in the event of a charge being laid. Under the law as it is, if there is a charge in the books it can be proved by affidavit, but when there is nothing we have had to bring witnesses to court.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Right Hon. ERNEST LAPOINTE (Minister of Justice) moved that the house go into committee to consider the following proposed resolution:
That it is expedient to amend the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Act to provide that time served in the permanent naval, military and air forces of Canada may be included in the term of service of an officer or a constable for pension purposes; and to restrict the application of the act in respect to members of the reserve.
Motion agreed to and the house went into committee, Mr. Johnston (Lake Centre) in the chair.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: PERMANENT MILITARY AND AIR FORCE SERVICE TO BE INCLUDED FOR PENSION PURPOSES
speechtext:
There are two main amendments in the bill which will be introduced. As the law now stands, it
provides that the time served in the permanent forces of Canada may be included in the term of service of an officer for the purposes of pension under this part. This amendment inserts the words, "naval, military or air" in the expression, "permanent forces of Canada." It has not been clear under existing statutory definitions that the expression "permanent forces of Canada" included the naval and air forces as well as the military. It has always been the intention to include this service.
The other amendment has to do with reservists of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PERMANENT MILITARY AND AIR FORCE SERVICE TO BE INCLUDED FOR PENSION PURPOSES
speechtext: They were provided for last year.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: PERMANENT MILITARY AND AIR FORCE SERVICE TO BE INCLUDED FOR PENSION PURPOSES
speechtext:
We enacted the following clause:
Every member of such reserve on being called up for duty or training will be subject to this act, and all rules and regulations made thereunder from the date of his being called up, which date shall be the day on which he is advised by registered letter to report himself for duty.
We desire to restrict the application of this section. For instance, it is not desired that a reservist should be entitled to all the benefits of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Act such as pensions, etc., unless he is injured or killed on duty. Under the section enacted last year the reservists were entitled to all the privileges of the permanent police force, and this is to restrict the application of the section to when they are injured or killed on duty.
Resolution reported, read the second time and concurred in. Mr. Lapointe (Quebec East) thereupon moved for leave to introduce Bill No. 40, to amend the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Act.
Motion agreed to and bill read the first time.

I have every sympathy for the request made by my hon. friend. I know no man in this house has taken more interest in the veterans generally than he has, and I know he wants to see something done particularly for those in the interior. Since he last brought the matter to our attention we have given it considerable study and we find that we are up to date in the work in British Columbia. A quorum has been in session at Vancouver and Victoria for several months and is just now about to proceed to points in the interior. This quorum will hold a session at Kamloops on April 6, after which it will visit Revelstoke, Vernon, Nelson and Cran-brook. Some fifteen entitlement applications will be heard at these points together with a few miscellaneous cases. On completion of these sittings, the only entitlement cases awaiting quorum hearing in the interior of British Columbia will be one at Prince George and two at Prince Rupert.
The work in hand in British Columbia does not warrant the appointment of an additional advocate. We already have Mr. Walter Drin-nan and Mr. D. F. Markland at Vancouver and Mr. G. H. Sedger at Victoria. We formerly had four advocates in British Columbia, Mr. E. S. Keeling having been on the staff at Vancouver. This advocate, however, resigned some little time ago and has not been replaced because the work in hand did not warrant his replacement. Mr. Markland. who formerly lived at Fernie, has been specially detailed to look after the work at interior points. He is in the interior at the present time interviewing applicants and witnesses and otherwise making arrangements for the quorum sittings mentioned above. We have constantly sent Mr. Markland on trips through the interior to interview applicants, to give information and generally to render any service he can. His visits are always organized in advance; the officials of veterans' organizations at each point are notified of proposed visits; lists of applicants who want to interview the advocate are compiled, and the advocate takes with him a summary of the record. It is under this item that I am prepared to discuss anything connected with unemployment of ex-service men, and incidentally discuss the veterans' assistance commission report, the so-called Rattray report. I understand some of my hon. friends would like me to make some statement with respect to the attitude which we intend to adopt in connection with the report. I do not want to lead the committee into error. Properly speaking, as is known to most hon. members, the unemployment assistance provided under this vote really applies only to pensioners, but in order to have an appropriate item under which to discuss the case of non-

Supply-Pensions-Unemployment
pensioners who are unemployed I have suggested to certain hon. members that that discussion take place on this item.
The veterans' assistance commission was set up in July, 1936. It operated until January 6, 1938. It toured the whole country and obtained all available information with respect to unemployment and kindred matters as relating to ex-service men. A report was filed with the department, which has been printed in blue-book form and has been tabled and placed in the hands of all hon. members.
The commission in that report made a number of recommendations. I propose to deal with them one by one. The first recommendation, found on page 65, deals with workshops. It recommends:
Workshops
Whilst it is agreed that the operation of workshops can be considered only as in its experimental stages and whilst appreciating the fact that owing to local conditions it might not be possible to establish workshops in all the important cities in Canada, yet the commission believes that it is justified in recommending :
That favourable consideration be given to any applications for assistance that might be received from the management of any workshop now in existence, or under consideration, providing that it can be shown that the workshop is justifying its existence in the community and that the continued employment of veterans in the workshop is necessary and the objective of revolving labour is being carried out.
This recommendation has been implemented as provision has been made in the estimates for the continuation of the workshops which were commenced by the veterans' assistance commission in Montreal and Regina; also for limited assistance, if necessary, to the workshop project in operation at Moose Jaw.
Montreal
The Montreal workshop was started in January, 1937, and the grants to date to finance its operations amount to $55,000. Eighty men are at present on the pay roll, and 329 men have graduated, through the workshop, to permanent employment in other organizations. This is the valuable feature and the primary objective of the workshop.
An employment division is operated in connection with the workshop and the honorary local committee, with the following results:
